title: Dhamaal 4 Wraps Theatrical Run at ₹160 Crore in India, Declared a Clean Hit
excerpt: Ajay Devgn's comedy franchise closer finishes as Bollywood's fourth hit of 2026, crossing ₹224 crore worldwide and cementing its place as the actor's sixth-highest-grossing film ever.
body:
• Dhamaal 4 has closed its Indian theatrical run at approximately ₹160.50 crore nett (₹192.60 crore gross), earning a Clean Hit verdict at the box office.
  • The film's total worldwide gross stands at approximately ₹224.54 crore, including ₹29.61 crore from overseas markets.
  • Directed by Indra Kumar, it becomes the fourth Bollywood hit of 2026 after Border 2, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, and Bhooth Bangla.
  • Ajay Devgn's next release, Drishyam 3: The Conclusion, is set to arrive in cinemas on October 2, 2026.

Final Box Office Numbers

Dhamaal 4, the fourth installment in Indra Kumar's slapstick comedy franchise, has effectively completed its theatrical run in India. The Ajay Devgn-starrer collected approximately ₹160.50 crore nett (₹192.60 crore gross) domestically over six weeks, according to Pinkvilla, falling just short of the heights its opening weekend had suggested but comfortably earning a Clean Hit verdict.

Adding overseas earnings of approximately ₹29.61 crore gross, the film's total worldwide collection stands at roughly ₹224.54 crore, according to data compiled by Wikipedia and Bollywood Hungama.

A Strong Start That Gradually Tapered

The comedy entertainer opened to ₹13.75 crore on its first day, July 10, before climbing through the weekend—₹22.48 crore on Saturday and ₹28.15 crore on Sunday—to post a domestic opening weekend of ₹64.35 crore nett. Week 1 closed at approximately ₹95-96 crore, a franchise-best start.

The second week added ₹38.50-40.65 crore, keeping the film firmly in the conversation. However, the arrival of major Hollywood releases—first The Odyssey, then Spider-Man: Brand New Day—progressively ate into screen allocations and showings. Week 3 contributed ₹17.75 crore, and the fourth weekend yielded ₹4.65 crore as the film entered its final stretch.

Franchise Performance and Bollywood Context

Dhamaal 4 becomes Ajay Devgn's sixth-highest-grossing film ever at the worldwide box office. The franchise, which began with 2007's Dhamaal and continued through Double Dhamaal (2011) and Total Dhamaal (2019), has proven its durability as a Bollywood comedy brand across nearly two decades.

The film outperformed Akshay Kumar's Welcome To The Jungle, another franchise comedy released earlier in 2026, though industry analysts note that Welcome To The Jungle faced stiffer competition throughout its run. Dhamaal 4 benefited from three relatively clear weeks before Spider-Man: Brand New Day arrived on July 31.

"Dhamaal 4 turned out to be a Clean Hit venture at the box office. It is the fourth HIT of the year for Bollywood, after Border 2, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, and Bhooth Bangla."

— Pinkvilla

The film's success is notable given persistent discussion about franchise fatigue in Bollywood. After several franchise sequels underperformed in 2025, Dhamaal 4 joined Border 2, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, and Bhooth Bangla as proof that established properties can still deliver when execution and timing align.

What's Next for Ajay Devgn

With Dhamaal 4's theatrical journey complete, attention now shifts to Ajay Devgn's next major release: Drishyam 3: The Conclusion. The final chapter of the critically acclaimed Drishyam franchise is set for an October 2, 2026 release—a date that historically performs well at the Indian box office.

For Indra Kumar, Dhamaal 4's commercial performance validates the decision to revive the franchise after a five-year gap. The ensemble cast—featuring Riteish Deshmukh, Arshad Warsi, Jaaved Jaaferi, Esha Gupta, Sanjay Mishra, and Ravi Kishan alongside Devgn—delivered the kind of broad-audience entertainment that continues to find its market in Indian cinemas.
